title: Journey (band)
wiki_lead:
Journey is an American rock band formed in San Francisco in 1973 by former members of Santana, the Steve Miller Band, and Frumious Bandersnatch. The band as of 2026 consists of Neal Schon on guitars and vocals; Jonathan Cain on keyboards, guitars and vocals; Deen Castronovo on drums and vocals; Arnel Pineda on lead vocals; Jason Derlatka on keyboards and vocals; and Todd Jensen on bass and vocals.
Journey had their biggest commercial success between 1978 and 1987, when Steve Perry was lead vocalist; they released a series of hit songs, including "Don't Stop Believin'" (1981). In 2024, the track was certified 18-times platinum by the RIAA, surpassing all previous records to become the top-selling digital track in US history. Escape, Journey's seventh and most successful album, reached number one on the Billboard 200 and yielded another of their most popular singles, "Open Arms". The 1983 follow-up album, Frontiers, was almost as successful in the United States, reaching number two and spawning several successful singles; it broadened the band's appeal in the United Kingdom, where it reached number six on the UK Albums Chart. Journey enjoyed a successful reunion in the mid-1990s with the album Trial by Fire (1996), and have since regrouped twice; first with Steve Augeri from 1998 to 2006, then with Arnel Pineda from 2007 onward.
Sales have resulted in 25 gold and platinum albums, in addition to the 18-time platinum RIAA Diamond Certified, 1988's Greatest Hits album. They have had 19 top-40 singles in the US, six of which reached the top 10 of the US chart and two of which reached number one on other Billboard charts, and a number-six hit on the UK Singles Chart in "Don't Stop Believin'". Originally a progressive rock band, Journey was described by AllMusic as having cemented a reputation as "one of America's most beloved (and sometimes hated) commercial rock/pop bands" by 1978, when they redefined their sound by embracing pop arrangements on their fourth album, Infinity.

History


1973–1977: Formation, Journey, Look into the Future and Next

The original members of Journey came together in San Francisco in 1973 under the auspices of former Santana manager Herbie Herbert. Originally called the Golden Gate Rhythm Section and intended to serve as a backup group for established Bay Area artists, the band included Santana alumni Neal Schon on lead guitar and Gregg Rolie on keyboards and lead vocals. Bassist Ross Valory, formerly of both Frumious Bandersnatch and the Steve Miller Band, as well as rhythm guitarist George Tickner of Frumious Bandersnatch rounded out the group. Prairie Prince of The Tubes served as drummer. After one performance in Hawaii, the band quickly abandoned the "backup group" concept and developed a distinctive jazz fusion style. After an unsuccessful radio contest to name the group, roadie John Villanueva suggested the name "Journey".

grok_lead: Journey is an American rock band formed in San Francisco in 1973 by former members of Santana and Frumious Bandersnatch, including guitarist Neal Schon and keyboardist Gregg Rolie. Best known for their anthemic arena rock sound and soaring power ballads, Journey rose to international prominence in the late 1970s and 1980s, particularly after vocalist Steve Perry joined in 1977. The band has sold over 100 million albums worldwide and was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2017. Initially blending progressive rock, jazz fusion, and hard rock influences, Journey signed with Columbia Records in 1974 and released their self-titled debut album in 1975, which peaked at No. 138 on the Billboard 200. Early lineups featured Schon on guitar, Rolie on keyboards and vocals, bassist Ross Valory, drummer Aynsley Dunbar (later replaced by Steve Smith), and various vocalists before Perry's arrival transformed their style toward more accessible, radio-friendly melodies. Their breakthrough came with albums like Infinity (1978), Evolution (1979), and especially Escape (1981), which topped the Billboard 200 and spawned massive hits including "Don't Stop Believin'"âcertified 18Ã Platinum by the RIAA and one of the best-selling digital tracks ever with over seven million downloads. Journey's commercial peak continued through the 1980s with multi-platinum releases such as Frontiers (1983) and the 18Ã Platinum-certified Greatest Hits (1988), which has sold 18 million copies in the U.S. alone, earning them 25 gold and platinum albums and 19 Top 40 singles. Keyboardist Jonathan Cain joined in 1980, contributing to songwriting hits like "Open Arms" and "Faithfully," while the band's dynamic live performances filled stadiums worldwide. After Perry's departure in 1987 due to health issues, the band experimented with replacements and hiatuses, releasing Trial by Fire (1996)âwhich earned a Grammy nominationâand undergoing further lineup changes, including the 2020 exit of Valory and Smith amid internal disputes. In 2007, Filipino vocalist Arnel Pineda joined after being discovered via YouTube, revitalizing Journey for a new generation and leading to successful tours. The band received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 2005 and the Billboard Legend of Live Award in 2011, cementing their legacy as enduring rock icons. As of November 2025, Journeyâfeaturing Schon, Cain (who announced in October 2025 his departure after the upcoming tour), Pineda, bassist Todd Jensen, drummer Deen Castronovo, and keyboardist Jason Derlatkaâhas announced their farewell "Final Frontier Tour," scheduled to begin in February 2026 and span 60 dates across North America through July. With 15 studio albums to their name, Journey remains a cornerstone of classic rock, their music enduring through film soundtracks, covers, and cultural revivals like the 2007 The Sopranos finale boost for "Don't Stop Believin'."
